priceSnapshot.note: Against the endday mark of 64,694.1 the tape is UP 0.24%. The overnight did exactly what a healthy consolidation does: it dipped first to 64,444.4 at 03:00Z, then rebuilt and tagged 65,000.0 on the 05:00Z hour before settling back to 64,850. Session range measured since the endday snapshot (00:45Z onward, from the 15m series): low 64,444.4, high 65,000.0 - a 555.6-point band, 0.37 of a daily ATR. Two things matter about that range. The endday's 64,110 reduce trigger was never approached - the low held 334 points clear of it - and the endday's recommended stop at 64,020 was never touched. The 65,000 handle rejected for a third time in 24 hours, 26.6 points under the 24-hour high of 65,026.6.

Those two lines have converged to within 4 points of each other, so a single close below takes out both at once and there is no second chance beneath. That is the floor of the entire reclaim thesis - it has now held on a closing basis for five consecutive UTC days. The intermediate warnings between spot and it are the 1h EMA20 at 64,631.82, the overnight low at 64,444.4, and the 1h EMA50 at 64,330.87.

addIf.confirmation: A 4H CLOSE above $65,030, which clears the 24-hour high of 65,026.6 and the 65,000 handle that has now rejected three separate times inside 24 hours - at 16:15 COT yesterday, at 20:00Z, and again at 05:00Z this morning. A wick through it is not the signal; the 4H close is, because each of those three rejections happened intrabar. Above it the next measured objects are the 31 Jul swing high at 65,423.7 and then a long air pocket up to the daily EMA100 at 67,049.47.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from the endday's REDUCE back to ADD, and the reason is that the exact condition the endday named has resolved bullish. The endday flagged one thing above all others to re-check at midnight: the 05 Aug Farside row was incomplete at +47.6M with the IBIT column still a dash, and it warned that a negative IBIT would break the three-day inflow streak and put the 64,110 line in play. The row has now completed. IBIT printed +196.8M and the 05 Aug total is +244.4M - not a deceleration but the LARGEST day of the streak, running 170.1, 211.5, 244.4. The endday's trim was correct risk management for an unknown; the unknown has been answered, so the dry powder goes back to work. The stop recommendation flips from true to false: the endday needed one because the next report was thirteen hours away, whereas the morning session is roughly 4.7 hours out and price sits 725 points above the trigger.

liquidation.note: $1,990,962 of REALIZED liquidations bucketed into the 64,850-64,950 band, the single heaviest cluster anywhere in the 22-hour window, and it sits 50 points above spot. This is where the market has ALREADY paid, which is a different object from a forward heatmap: it marks the price band that has been most expensive to be wrong at, and it explains why the last three pushes into 65,000 all stalled within 150 points of here.

$1,457,075 of realized liquidations in the 64,750-64,850 band, immediately beneath spot. Taken with the 64,900 cluster this is one continuous 200-point zone carrying $3.45M of the $7.94M total - roughly 43% of everything liquidated in the window sits within 100 points of the current price. That density is why the tape has been chopping here rather than trending.

$1,111,686 of realized liquidations in the 64,650-64,750 band. It brackets the daily EMA50 at 64,672.97 and the 15m EMA50 at 64,686.04, so a flush into it would be testing measured moving-average support and a measured liquidation shelf at the same price.

$997,734 of realized liquidations in the 64,450-64,550 band, sitting right on the overnight low of 64,444.4 and just above the 15m EMA100 at 64,555.23. This is the first genuine shelf beneath the current chop zone, 350 points down or 0.23 of a daily ATR.

$527,164 of realized liquidations in the 64,350-64,450 band, straddling the overnight low. Beneath it the surface thins sharply - 64,300 carries only $146,837 and 64,200 only $36,649 - so a loss of 64,400 opens a comparatively empty stretch down toward the daily/4H EMA20 pair at 64,122-64,126.

liquidityMagnet.note: The pull reads UP on composition rather than distance. Of the $7,943,441 liquidated in the window, $6,978,567 (87.9%) was SHORTS being bought back and only $964,873 (12.1%) was longs being sold. A tape that liquidates shorts eight-to-one while grinding higher is a tape where the marginal forced order is a buy. The two nearest clusters straddle spot almost symmetrically - 64,900 above, 64,800 below - so distance gives no edge either way; what tilts it is that the side which keeps getting carried out is the short side. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON WHAT THIS IS: these are REALIZED liquidations, a record of where leverage has already died, not a forward-looking heatmap of resting stops. It is directionally informative and it is measured rather than estimated, but it is a rear-view mirror. No CoinGlass forward heatmap was read this run because the OKX feed came back fresh and verifiable and there was no need for the browser fallback.

calibration.rollingRecord: The endday scored well on direction and levels and poorly on the one decision it actually made. Its 64,110 reduce trigger was NOT approached - the overnight low of 64,444.4 held 334 points clear - so priorReduceFired is false and the decision to place the trigger at the daily EMA20 rather than a round number was vindicated. Its recommended stop at 64,020 was never touched. Its 65,110 add trigger was NOT reached either: the overnight high was 65,000.0, 110 points short, so the session correctly refused an add it had not earned. Direction was right - price is 155.6 points higher at 64,849.7, up 0.24% from the endday mark, and the bullish-leaning 46/36/18 split paid. But actingHelped is FALSE, and it should be recorded honestly: the endday trimmed 10% of the spot core at 64,694.1 and price is now higher, so the trim cost roughly 0.04 USDT of foregone gain on the sold portion. It was defensible risk management into a thirteen-hour gap with an unresolved ETF print, and this session is buying the tranche back, but the trade itself did not make money.
calibration.note: One pattern worth carrying forward. The endday named a SPECIFIC, FALSIFIABLE overnight condition - 'if IBIT lands negative when the row completes, the streak breaks and 64,110 gets tested' - rather than a vague risk warning. That is what made this session's job easy: the row completed at IBIT +196.8M and total +244.4M, the condition resolved to the bullish side, and the position could flip from REDUCE back to ADD in one step with a documented reason instead of a re-argued thesis. Sessions should keep naming the single binary that decides the next call. The other carry-forward is mechanical and now proven twice: OKX served four different data vintages through the fetch proxy yesterday, and every one of the same endpoints came back live today when called same-origin from inside the browser. The access path, not the exchange, was the stale-data problem.
